### C. Counts and coverage

MVP-live: 168 criteria (auto 136, lint 18, review 8, manual 6); deferred: 27 (auto 18, review 3, manual 6); total 195. Counted mechanically from the tag of each criterion (first tag word; a tag containing `deferred` counts as deferred wherever it sits, a B-section tag marked `live` counts as live, and the retired row is not counted) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G1/G4/G6: AC-SN-181 (auto) and AC-SN-182 (auto, integration) added live; clauses edited inside AC-SN-25, 123, 150 and 151 change no count; the earlier count was 166 live, 27 deferred, 193 total)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: AC-SN-180 added live auto; clauses edited inside AC-SN-3, 11, 45, 50, 59, 64, 74, 97, 133, 136, 150, 158, 162 and 174 change no count; the earlier count was 165 live, 27 deferred, 192 total)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: AC-SN-36b, 173, 174, 175, 178 added live auto, AC-SN-176 and 179 added live lint, AC-SN-177 added deferred auto; AC-SN-70, 90 and 91 re-tagged auto to review (live), AC-SN-102 re-tagged auto to review (deferred) and AC-SN-106 re-tagged manual to auto (deferred); the earlier count was 158 live, 26 deferred, 184 total, and the two retired ids AC-SN-43 and AC-SN-112 are not counted)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: AC-SN-171 added live and AC-SN-172 added deferred; the earlier count was 157 live, 25 deferred, 182 total)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: AC-SN-111 and AC-SN-114 moved from deferred to live, AC-SN-112 retired, AC-SN-158 to 165, 169 and 170 added live, AC-SN-166 and 167 added deferred, AC-SN-168 added as a live manual ADVISORY row; the earlier count was 144 live, 26 deferred, 170 total)*. Coverage: every Core Rule SN-1 to SN-30 and every formula D.1 to D.13 has at least one criterion (SN-5 and SN-6 via AC-SN-16, 23, 24, 2

### Gaps / untestable as written

- **Perf threshold (QA-14).** AC-SN-97 now asserts a provisional ceiling derived from the registered `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 (median at most 0.5 ms, maximum at most 2 ms) on a `template_release` export, with the first measured baseline kept as a ratchet; the reference machines are RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (delegated ruling R12, closes X14) and the ceiling is pending spike measurement on them; the technical-director confirms the 0.5 ms median and the percentile from that measurement (OQ-SN-19). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*
- **World-cost thresholds (QA-15).** AC-SN-71 and AC-SN-134 use 1000 hp and 15 s as placeholders; "non-trivial" and "costly but possible" have no designer-confirmed number (OQ-SN-18). The 15 s is bounded from below by the D.7 two-hop worst case (13.0 s) plus a 2 s margin and from above by `WITNESS_HOPS_MAX` 3 (17.5 s), so it is the derived consequence of two hops; the 1000 hp is **not derived** (the Graph's fault timelines give 192 bp per two minutes for a coolant leak and 4800 bp for a bus overload, so a single hp figure cannot hold for all eight faults) and the numeric clause of AC-SN-71 is therefore ADVISORY until each fault gets its own derived figure from its D.15 timeline. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED)*
- **D.13 (QA-6).** The 1500 AU bound fails for any phantom response above 8.33 s, which is 92 percent of the `PHANTOM_LIFE_S` 8 to 20 range; AC-SN-106 now evaluates the formula over the registry constants at 360, 500, 501 and 1200 ticks (the 8.33 s boundary and the 20 s life), and the 20 s case is OQ-SN-20. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED)*
- **AC-SN-71 manual half and AC-SN-88, AC-SN-148, AC-SN-165 and AC-SN-168** are playtest observations and cannot be automated; they are ADVISORY with sign-off. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-SN-64** asserts SIM data only; the Filter's non-reaction to the `away` flip is AC-PF-66b. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP, supersedes the 2026-10-27 delegated G1 listing rule)*
- **AC-SN-43 (retired).** The stale-token scan of the GDD text is a `/design-review` checklist item, not a game criterion: it is context-sensitive, so no mechanical oracle exists (QA-17). Its literal-scan half survives as AC-SN-42 and AC-SN-96.
- **GDScript behaviour is [UNV].** The engine reference has no scripting module file; integer overflow, signed-shift behaviour and Dictionary iteration order are unverified, which is why AC-SN-2 and AC-SN-76 assert sorted output and counters below 2^53.
- **Filter-dependent criteria.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: status refresh. The Perception Filter GDD exists, `perception-filter.md`, Designed; what is missing is a built Filter.)* No MVP-live criterion can render a lie until the Filter is built; AC-SN-140, 141, 149, 153, 154, 166 and 167 wait for it, and AC-SN-67 and AC-SN-83 run against whatever stand-in the vertical slice ships.

## Open Questions

Owner is `user` (a decision only the user, or the creative-director acting for the user, can take), `agent` (a specialist or sibling GDD) or `GDD` (this document, to be closed by its own rules). Target is `playtest`, `next GDD` or `ADR`. User-decision items come first. Ids are stable; closed ids are listed after the table.

| # | Question | Owner | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| OQ-SN-16 | Set `testing.strict.config: true` in `project.yaml` for the `sanity` data files? The data guards (AC-SN-45, 49, 50, 51, 86, 152) protect Pillars 1 and 4, and `/smoke-check` already defaults config to BLOCKING while per-story Config/Data evidence defaults to ADVISORY. Recommendation: yes. | user | ADR (project config) |
| OQ-SN-38 | **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): option (b).** `STAGE_ENTER[2]` is 55,000 (was 45,000) and `AMBIENT_FLOOR[1]` is 53,000 (was 62,000), with D.4 (i) to (v) and D.8 (a) to (e) re-run in full (all pass, margins unchanged; derivation and worked example in D.8). The MVP reachable stage envelope (SN-29 table) is recomputed: a calm ring-1 sortie is stage 0 for 315.8 s, stage 1 until 473.8 s and stage 2 after; ring 2 reaches stage 2 at 391.4 s and ring 3 at 333.4 s; stage 3 needs 3 to 5 breach epochs in rings 1 and 2 and 2 to 3 in ring 3. The per-home-ring rest budget the MVP assumes is the one computed in SN-29: from the ring-1 floor a ring-1 home reaches `SAN_MAX` in 13.1 min, ring 2 in 19.6 min, ring 3 in 39.2 min (replacing 10.6 / 15.8 / 31.7). Stage-2 D.7 rows and ACs are no longer forced-state only. Original question kept for the record: (a) stage 1 as the main band with INTENSE at VS-A, or (b) lower the ring-1 floor and the stage-2 threshold. | user (creative-director) | closed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |

The review's overlap premise with `DEBUNK_IMMUNE_S` did not hold (Interaction declined the repair-completion debunk, OQ-SN-12), but the level-designer's objection (it punishes the room the player is working in) carries the ruling; EC-SN-25 still allows a post-repair lie at the base rate. | user (creative-director) | closed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |

641	#### D.2 `stage_of`
642	
643	The `stage_of` formula is defined as:
644	
645	`stage' = stage_of(level, stage, stage_dwell)`: return `stage` while `stage_dwell < STAGE_DWELL_RUNS`; otherwise step `target` deeper while `level < STAGE_ENTER[target + 1]` (worsening is evaluated first), and only if it did not move, step `target` shallower while `level > STAGE_ENTER[target] + STAGE_HYST`
646	
647	The same rule as a step list (one transition per run, the deeper applying):
648	
649	```
650	if stage_dwell < STAGE_DWELL_RUNS: return stage
651	target = stage
652	while target < 3 and level < STAGE_ENTER[target + 1]: target += 1      # worsen first
653	if target == stage:
654	    while target > 0 and level > STAGE_ENTER[target] + STAGE_HYST: target -= 1
655	return target                                                          # caller resets stage_dwell to 0 on a change
656	```
657	
658	**Variables:**
659	
660	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
661	|---|---|---|---|---|
662	| `level` | int mSU | 0 to 100000 | `sanity.state` | level after D.1 |
663	| `stage` | int | 0 to 3 | `sanity.state` | stage before this run |
664	| `stage_dwell` | int runs | 0 to `STAGE_DWELL_RUNS` (saturating) | `sanity.state` | runs since the last change; +1 per run |
665	| `STAGE_ENTER[s]` | int mSU | 70000 / 55000 / 25000 for s = 1..3 | knob | entry thresholds, strictly below; stage 2 raised from 45000 by the user ruling on OQ-SN-38 (D.8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
666	| `STAGE_HYST` | int mSU | 2000 (safe 1000 to 2000; D.8 (b) caps it at 2000) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED)* | knob | the exit threshold of stage `s` is `STAGE_ENTER[s] + STAGE_HYST` (72000 / 57000 / 27000), strictly above *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
667	| `STAGE_DWELL_RUNS` | int runs | 25 (5 s; safe 10 to 50) | knob | minimum runs between changes |
668	
669	**Output Range:** an integer in 0 to 3; a stage 4 is impossible by construction. Entry is strictly below and exit strictly above, so `level` exactly 70000 stays stage 0 and exactly 72000 stays stage 1. Two thresholds cannot be crossed inside one dwell under the cap (`25 x 36` = 900 mSU against gaps of at least 15000, the 70000-to-55000 gap, after the OQ-SN-38 ruling); the only ways to see a jump of more than one stage are a restore (the stored stage is kept, no recompute) and a debug `force_*` (recompute with the dwell saturated, directly to the target).
670	**Example:** `level` 69964, `stage` 0, `stage_dwell` 25: 69964 < 70000 so `target` 1; 69964 is not < 55000, so stage 1 and the dwell resets. At 71000 the stage holds (71000 is not above 72000). At 72001 with the dwell back at 25, `target` 0. Direct drop: `stage` 2, `level` 57500, dwell 25: not worsening; 57500 > 57000 so `target` 1; 57500 is not > 72000 so it stops at 1. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
671	
672	#### D.3 `harm_gate`
673	
674	The `harm_gate` formula is defined as:
675	
676	`harm_below_runs' = (level < SAN_HARM_ENTER) ? min(SAN_HARM_DWELL_RUNS, harm_below_runs + 1) : 0` while not eligible; `harm_eligible' = harm_eligible ? (level <= SAN_HARM_EXIT) : (harm_below_runs' >= SAN_HARM_DWELL_RUNS)`; `tell_on' = (level < SAN_TELL_ON) ? true : (level > SAN_TELL_OFF) ? false : tell_on`
677	
678	**Variables:**
679	
680	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
681	|---|---|---|---|---|
682	| `SAN_HARM_ENTER` | int mSU | 15000 | knob | harm-gate entry threshold, strictly below |
683	| `SAN_HARM_EXIT` | int mSU | 20000 (> `SAN_HARM_ENTER`; safe 15612, the D.9 boot assertion, to 25000) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)* | knob | exit threshold, strictly above, clears at once |
684	| `SAN_HARM_DWELL_RUNS` | int runs | 150 (30 s; safe 122 to 300, D.4 (v)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED)* | knob | consecutive runs below `SAN_HARM_ENTER` needed |
685	| `harm_below_runs` | int runs | 0 to 150 | `sanity.state` | dwell counter; frozen at 150 while eligible and reset to 0 on clearing |
686	| `SAN_TELL_ON`, `SAN_TELL_OFF` | int mSU | 30000, 35000 (`SAN_TELL_OFF` > `SAN_TELL_ON`) | knobs | victim-tell flag thresholds; no dwell |
687	| `harm_eligible`, `tell_on` | bool | - | `sanity.state` | the two flags; `harm_eligible` is the single SIM bit the gate query and the class-(c) render read (SN-11) |
688	
689	**Output Range:** two booleans and a counter in 0 to 150. The earliest eligibility is 150 runs = 30 s after the first run below 15000. Outside debug force: `harm_eligible` implies `stage == 3` (eligibility needs the level below 20000 and stage 3 is held until 27000) and implies `tell_on` (cleared only above 35000), asserted at boot as corollaries of D.4.
690	**Example:** the level crosses 14990 at run n: counter 1; at run n + 149 the counter reaches 150 and the bit sets (30 s). If instead the level returns to exactly 15000 at run n + 60 (counter 60), the counter resets to 0 (a run at or above `SAN_HARM_ENTER` resets). Once eligible at 9600, recovery to 20001 clears the bit that run; at 20000 exactly it holds. `tell_on` sets at 29999 and, at 33000, stays set (inside the band).
691	
692	#### D.4 `drift_lead_invariant`
693	
694	The `drift_lead_invariant` formula is defined as:
695	
696	`lead_runs(a, b) = (a - b + DRIFT_MAX_PER_RUN - 1) div DRIFT_MAX_PER_RUN`; `lead_s(a, b) = lead_runs(a, b) x SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR / TICK_RATE`; build assertions (i) `lead_s(STAGE_ENTER[1], SAN_TELL_ON) >= SAN_STAGE1_TO_TELL_MIN_S`, (ii) `lead_s(SAN_TELL_ON, SAN_HARM_ENTER) >= SAN_TELL_LEAD_S`, (iii) `lead_s(STAGE_ENTER[1], SAN_HARM_ENTER) >= SAN_MIN_ONSET_TO_HARM_S`, (iv) `lead_s(SAN_TELL_ON, SAN_HARM_ENTER) + SAN_HARM_DWELL_RUNS x SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR / TICK_RATE >= SAN_TELL_LEAD_S`, **(v) `lead_s(min(AMBIENT_FLOOR), SAN_HARM_ENTER) + SAN_HARM_DWELL_RUNS x SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR / TICK_RATE >= SAN_FLOOR_TO_HARM_MIN_S`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: (v) is the lead measured from the lowest ambient floor, where routine play starts)*
697	
698	**Variables:**
699	
700	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
701	|---|---|---|---|---|
702	| `a`, `b` | int mSU | 0 to 100000 | knobs (thresholds) | upper and lower level of a bound |
703	| `DRIFT_MAX_PER_RUN` | int mSU/run | 36 | knob | the net cap, the worst-case descent rate |
704	| `SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR` | int ticks | 12 | equals the kernel divisor by relation (KRN:54, KRN:202); not a knob | ticks per run |
705	| `SAN_STAGE1_TO_TELL_MIN_S` | int s | 220 | knob | required stage-1 to `tell_on` lead |
706	| `SAN_TELL_LEAD_S` | int s | 60 (safe 45 to 83, one knob at a time, others at default) | knob | required `tell_on` to eligibility lead |
707	| `SAN_MIN_ONSET_TO_HARM_S` | int s | 300 (safe 240 to 305) | knob | required stage-1 entry to eligibility lead |
708	| `SAN_FLOOR_TO_HARM_MIN_S` | int s | 180 `[PLACEHOLDER]` value; the target is confirmed by the user ruling on OQ-SN-43 (2026-10-27: three minutes from routine ring-3 play to lethal friendly harm); safe 150 to 185 with the other knobs at their defaults *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED: upper end was 240)* | knob *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: new, registry request)* | required lead from the lowest ambient floor to eligibility, including the dwell |
709	| `min(AMBIENT_FLOOR)` | int mSU | 43000 | knob (SN-29) | the `a` of bound (v) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
710	| `STAGE_ENTER[1]`, `SAN_TELL_ON`, `SAN_HARM_ENTER` | int mSU | 70000, 30000, 15000 | knobs | the `a` and `b` of bounds (i) to (iv) |
711	| `SAN_HARM_DWELL_RUNS` | int runs | 150 | knob | the dwell added in bound (iv) |
712	
713	**Output Range:** pass or fail per bound. At the defaults:
714	
715	| Bound | Distance (mSU) | Runs at cap 36 | Seconds | Required | Margin |
716	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
717	| (i) 70000 to 30000 | 40000 | 1112 | 222.4 | 220 | 2.4 s |
718	| (ii) 30000 to 15000 | 15000 | 417 | 83.4 | 60 | 23.4 s |
719	| (iii) 70000 to 15000 | 55000 | 1528 | 305.6 (the bit sets on run 1677 = 335.4 s with the dwell, SN-10) | 300 | 5.6 s |
720	| (iv) `SAN_TELL_ON` to eligible, with the 150-run dwell | 15000 | 417 + 150 = 567 | 113.4 | 60 | 53.4 s |
721	| (v) lowest floor 43000 to eligible, with the dwell *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | 28000 | 778 + 150 = 928 | 185.6 | 180 | 5.6 s |
722	
723	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)* The same lead from the other floors, for reading only and not asserted: ring 2 (52000) 37000 mSU = 1028 + 150 runs = 235.6 s; ring 1 (53000) 38000 mSU = 1056 + 150 runs = 241.2 s (was 291.2 s from the 62000 floor before the OQ-SN-38 ruling). The lowest-floor case binds, so asserting it covers the others. **Re-run for the OQ-SN-38 pair** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: bounds (i) to (v) read only `STAGE_ENTER[1]` 70000, `SAN_TELL_ON` 30000, `SAN_HARM_ENTER` 15000, `min(AMBIENT_FLOOR)` 43000, the cap 36 and the dwell; none of them moved (the stage-2 entry and the ring-1 floor are not inputs of any bound), so every row of the table above and every margin (2.4, 23.4, 5.6, 53.4 and 5.6 s) is unchanged and all five pass. Closed form for (v): `DRIFT_MAX_PER_RUN < (min floor - SAN_HARM_ENTER) / (5 x (S_v - 30) - 1)` = `28000 / 749` = 37.4 with `S_v` 180, which the cap 36 passes, and `SAN_HARM_ENTER <= min floor - (749 x 36 + 1)` = 43000 - 26965 = 16035 (the same ceiling as bound (iii)).
724	
725	**Closed form for the cap.** Bound `i` needs `lead_runs >= 5 x S_i`, which holds exactly when `DRIFT_MAX_PER_RUN < d_i / (5 x S_i - 1)`: (i) `40000 / 1099` = 36.4, (ii) `15000 / 299` = 50.2, (iii) `55000 / 1499` = 36.7, so the largest passing cap is `min(36, 50, 36)` = 36 and 36 is the value used. At 37: (i) `ceil(40000 / 37)` = 1082 runs = 216.4 s fails, and (iii) `ceil(55000 / 37)` = 1487 runs = 297.4 s fails. (i) and (iii) bind together. **Cap-is-binding demonstration:** the uncapped `E - R` exceeds 36 in every danger state that matters: ring 3 aboard in BREACH with a horror near is `8 + 20 + 28 + 20 - 1` = 75; without the horror `8 + 20 + 28 - 1` = 55; ring 1 aboard in BREACH `0 + 20 + 28 - 1` = 47; ring 1 aboard in a tier-3 TELL `0 + 20 + 20 - 1` = 39; a tier-2 TELL aboard (`0 + 20 + 12 - 1` = 31) is the first state below the cap. **Example:** raise the cap to 40 with nothing else changed: (iii) gives `ceil(55000 / 40)` = 1375 runs = 275.0 s against 300 s, failing; the boot assertion refuses with `SANITY_BOOT_LEAD_INVARIANT`. Any retune of a threshold, the cap, the divisor, an exposure rate or an ambient floor re-runs all five (reflexion P-2, P-7). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)*

findings.section: Tuning Knobs L1114 / Formulas D.1 table L613 / SN-29 calibration L385 / registry ABOARD_EXPOSURE unit text (entities.yaml ~L10631) / AC-SN-171 (L1790)
findings.finding: Carried over a second time (G3). ABOARD_EXPOSURE is still published as 'safe 8 to 20' in four places, but D.8's derivation (L848) says the user-ruled stage-2 reach fails for any ABOARD_EXPOSURE below 12 at the 14-minute visit. At 8, net is 7 and stage 2 needs 21.4 minutes. A tuner following the published safe range breaks the user-ruled reach silently. AC-SN-171 does catch it, but only as a test failure named STAGE2_UNREACHABLE, which is not in the closed SANITY_BOOT_REASONS set (registry L1170). The AC does not say it is a test-time oracle name and not a boot reason.
findings.fix: Change the safe range to 12 to 20 in L613, L385, L1114 and the registry unit text, or keep 8 to 20 and mark 8 to 11 'breaks stage-2 reach; re-run AC-SN-171'. In AC-SN-171 state that STAGE2_UNREACHABLE is a test-failure label, not a SANITY_BOOT_* reason. Alternatively add a boot assertion _STAGE2_REACH to the closed set.

findings.finding: Still reads 'each routed refresh C1 to C30' and 'no neighbour file was edited by this stage'. The Cross-References table runs to C34, and the G6 pass deliberately edited the siblings (Suit SE-40, Perception Filter, Debug Overlay and others). As written the AC cannot pass.
findings.fix: Rewrite as: 'GIVEN the Cross-References refresh table WHEN reviewed THEN every C-id C1 to C34 (and any later id) has a recorded status, owed or closed, and an owner; ids closed by the 2026-10-28 cross-GDD pass cite the sibling section that closed them. The AC does not assert the absence of neighbour edits.'

findings.section: Registry SAN_HARM_EXIT (entities.yaml L10550) vs D.9 / D.3 (L683, L864)
findings.finding: The registry unit text still says the range floor is 15360. D.9 recomputed the boot-assertion minimum as 15612 (17 runs x 36 + 15000). A value between 15360 and 15611 passes the registry range and fails SANITY_BOOT_HARM_HYSTERESIS. The GDD is the registry source, so the registry must conform (G1).
findings.fix: Change the registry range text to '15612 (D.9 boot assertion) to 25000'.

findings.section: Sibling save-load-and-versioned-format.md L303 vs Sanity C34 / registry SANITY_RESTORE_REASONS (L1183)
findings.finding: The Save/Load registry row for sanity.state still lists SUBJECT_UNRESOLVED in the closed SANITY_RESTORE_* set. Sanity (the source) and the registry retired it in the 2026-10-27 design review, so a well-formed dead subject_ref is INVALIDATED by the next hook run. Save/Load would implement a restore failure path that Sanity forbids. C34 is still open.
findings.fix: Edit Save/Load L303 to the seven-reason set (SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED, SHAPE, LEVEL_RANGE, STAGE_RANGE, COUNTER_RANGE, LIE_KIND_UNKNOWN, LIE_TIME_ORDER), then mark C34 closed in Sanity.

findings.finding: The new timing note says carried_instance and tool_held are 'the value committed by the most recent suit.vitals run, 4 ticks before the Sanity run (up to 10 ticks old)'. Suit SE-13 and the mutator table (L335) show carried_id is written by Interaction's pickup/drop apply (set_carried / release_carried), and tool_held is derived on read from suit.state.tools. Neither is committed by suit.vitals. interaction.step runs before sanity.drift on every tick, so Sanity sees the current value with no staleness. The note sends an implementer to the wrong hook and the wrong tolerance (a lie could appear a pickup-width late).
findings.fix: Replace the timing sentence with: 'read as of the end of interaction.step on the Sanity tick; no stale tolerance applies to these two reads (the suit.vitals stale-tolerant edge covers only the band and cue reads)'.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-SN-60 (L1684) vs SN-16 gate order (L293)
findings.finding: The AC says the fourth and fifth candidates 'are refused by the gap gate and then the cap'. L293 fixes the order cap (gate 4) before gap (gate 5). After the third candidate is accepted the one slot is full, so the cap refuses both first. The no-draw and no-counter outcome is identical, but any test asserting the refusal reason, or a telemetry code, would pin the wrong gate.
findings.fix: Change to 'the fourth and fifth are refused by the cap (gate 4) with no draw and no counter advance; the gap gate is only reached when headroom remains'.

findings.finding: Last Verified (2026-10-27) lags Last Updated (2026-10-28). The CD-GDD-ALIGN note says approved 2026-10-26 and must be re-run, but it has now been through several restagings. The file is about 560 KB with inline '(Amended ...)' history. This is the root cause of the carry-overs that survived two passes (AC-SN-25, 151, 123 and the ABOARD range), so another carry-over is likely until it is consolidated.
findings.fix: Set Last Verified to the date of this review. Re-run CD-GDD-ALIGN on the current text before sprint planning. Move amendment history into the review log or a changelog appendix and leave normative text only in the body.

findings.section: Formulas D.3 harm_gate (L676) vs States table (L447) and variables (L685)
findings.finding: The harm_below_runs expression is only defined 'while not eligible'. On the clearing run (eligible, level > 20000) the expression leaves the counter at 150, but the States table and the variable table say 0 on clearing. The value is persisted and hashed, and no AC covers the clearing run. Two implementations can differ on state_hash for one run.
findings.fix: Add a clearing branch to the D.3 expression (harm_below_runs' = 0 when eligible' is false and the actor was eligible). Add a boundary AC: eligible at level 20001 gives harm_eligible false and harm_below_runs 0 that run (G5).

findings.finding: It asserts identical lie draws after a death restore, quit restore or different restore_reason, with 'the same actions on a subject'. The lie draw stream keys on world_seed and per-subject counters, not on restore_epoch, so the AC is consistent with R1/R13. But under the real Attention and Horror, a death restore changes threat draws. That changes tell timing and level, and so the stage at which a lit-entry event arrives. A tester under the real Attention could see different gating with the same actions.
findings.fix: Add 'with Attention and Horror stubbed to a fixed phase script, or with the level and stage forced equal' to the GIVEN. Add 'counters are never read from restore_epoch'.

findings.finding: R12 says a pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling on RM-DESKTOP (16.6 ms) and RM-DECK (33.3 ms). The AC measures median, p99 and maximum but asserts only the median (<= 0.5 ms) and maximum (<= 2 ms) ceilings, with no p99 or frame-headroom assertion. The values stay pending spike measurement, which is intentional.
findings.fix: State that the frame P99 headroom of R12 (>= 1.7 ms desktop, >= 3.3 ms Deck) is checked by the Pipeline/Kernel perf AC and that this AC only gates Sanity's own step share. Alternatively add a Sanity p99 ceiling placeholder.

findings.finding: The 'was:' comment says 'the repaired_recent stamp is still written, re-enable post-MVP'. Next to the live entry_fields tail ('repaired_recent[] reserved, always empty at MVP', L1027) and G2 this reads as a contradiction. It is a history comment and the live value is correct (value 1).
findings.fix: Reword the comment to 'repaired_recent[] is reserved and written only post-MVP from a Graph repair event (OQ-SN-46)'.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs L1114 / Formulas D.1 table L613 / SN-29 calibration L385 / registry ABOARD_EXPOSURE unit text (entities.yaml ~L10631) / AC-SN-171 (L1790)
findings.finding: Carried over a second time (G3). ABOARD_EXPOSURE is still published as 'safe 8 to 20' in four places, but D.8's derivation (L848) says the user-ruled stage-2 reach fails for any ABOARD_EXPOSURE below 12 at the 14-minute visit. At 8, net is 7 and stage 2 needs 21.4 minutes. A tuner following the published safe range breaks the user-ruled reach silently. AC-SN-171 does catch it, but only as a test failure named STAGE2_UNREACHABLE, which is not in the closed SANITY_BOOT_REASONS set (registry L1170). The AC does not say it is a test-time oracle name and not a boot reason.
findings.fix: Change the safe range to 12 to 20 in L613, L385, L1114 and the registry unit text, or keep 8 to 20 and mark 8 to 11 'breaks stage-2 reach; re-run AC-SN-171'. In AC-SN-171 state that STAGE2_UNREACHABLE is a test-failure label, not a SANITY_BOOT_* reason. Alternatively add a boot assertion _STAGE2_REACH to the closed set.

findings.finding: Still reads 'each routed refresh C1 to C30' and 'no neighbour file was edited by this stage'. The Cross-References table runs to C34, and the G6 pass deliberately edited the siblings (Suit SE-40, Perception Filter, Debug Overlay and others). As written the AC cannot pass.
findings.fix: Rewrite as: 'GIVEN the Cross-References refresh table WHEN reviewed THEN every C-id C1 to C34 (and any later id) has a recorded status, owed or closed, and an owner; ids closed by the 2026-10-28 cross-GDD pass cite the sibling section that closed them. The AC does not assert the absence of neighbour edits.'

findings.section: Registry SAN_HARM_EXIT (entities.yaml L10550) vs D.9 / D.3 (L683, L864)
findings.finding: The registry unit text still says the range floor is 15360. D.9 recomputed the boot-assertion minimum as 15612 (17 runs x 36 + 15000). A value between 15360 and 15611 passes the registry range and fails SANITY_BOOT_HARM_HYSTERESIS. The GDD is the registry source, so the registry must conform (G1).
findings.fix: Change the registry range text to '15612 (D.9 boot assertion) to 25000'.

findings.section: Sibling save-load-and-versioned-format.md L303 vs Sanity C34 / registry SANITY_RESTORE_REASONS (L1183)
findings.finding: The Save/Load registry row for sanity.state still lists SUBJECT_UNRESOLVED in the closed SANITY_RESTORE_* set. Sanity (the source) and the registry retired it in the 2026-10-27 design review, so a well-formed dead subject_ref is INVALIDATED by the next hook run. Save/Load would implement a restore failure path that Sanity forbids. C34 is still open.
findings.fix: Edit Save/Load L303 to the seven-reason set (SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED, SHAPE, LEVEL_RANGE, STAGE_RANGE, COUNTER_RANGE, LIE_KIND_UNKNOWN, LIE_TIME_ORDER), then mark C34 closed in Sanity.

findings.finding: The new timing note says carried_instance and tool_held are 'the value committed by the most recent suit.vitals run, 4 ticks before the Sanity run (up to 10 ticks old)'. Suit SE-13 and the mutator table (L335) show carried_id is written by Interaction's pickup/drop apply (set_carried / release_carried), and tool_held is derived on read from suit.state.tools. Neither is committed by suit.vitals. interaction.step runs before sanity.drift on every tick, so Sanity sees the current value with no staleness. The note sends an implementer to the wrong hook and the wrong tolerance (a lie could appear a pickup-width late).
findings.fix: Replace the timing sentence with: 'read as of the end of interaction.step on the Sanity tick; no stale tolerance applies to these two reads (the suit.vitals stale-tolerant edge covers only the band and cue reads)'.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-SN-60 (L1684) vs SN-16 gate order (L293)
findings.finding: The AC says the fourth and fifth candidates 'are refused by the gap gate and then the cap'. L293 fixes the order cap (gate 4) before gap (gate 5). After the third candidate is accepted the one slot is full, so the cap refuses both first. The no-draw and no-counter outcome is identical, but any test asserting the refusal reason, or a telemetry code, would pin the wrong gate.
findings.fix: Change to 'the fourth and fifth are refused by the cap (gate 4) with no draw and no counter advance; the gap gate is only reached when headroom remains'.

findings.finding: Last Verified (2026-10-27) lags Last Updated (2026-10-28). The CD-GDD-ALIGN note says approved 2026-10-26 and must be re-run, but it has now been through several restagings. The file is about 560 KB with inline '(Amended ...)' history. This is the root cause of the carry-overs that survived two passes (AC-SN-25, 151, 123 and the ABOARD range), so another carry-over is likely until it is consolidated.
findings.fix: Set Last Verified to the date of this review. Re-run CD-GDD-ALIGN on the current text before sprint planning. Move amendment history into the review log or a changelog appendix and leave normative text only in the body.

findings.section: Formulas D.3 harm_gate (L676) vs States table (L447) and variables (L685)
findings.finding: The harm_below_runs expression is only defined 'while not eligible'. On the clearing run (eligible, level > 20000) the expression leaves the counter at 150, but the States table and the variable table say 0 on clearing. The value is persisted and hashed, and no AC covers the clearing run. Two implementations can differ on state_hash for one run.
findings.fix: Add a clearing branch to the D.3 expression (harm_below_runs' = 0 when eligible' is false and the actor was eligible). Add a boundary AC: eligible at level 20001 gives harm_eligible false and harm_below_runs 0 that run (G5).

findings.finding: It asserts identical lie draws after a death restore, quit restore or different restore_reason, with 'the same actions on a subject'. The lie draw stream keys on world_seed and per-subject counters, not on restore_epoch, so the AC is consistent with R1/R13. But under the real Attention and Horror, a death restore changes threat draws. That changes tell timing and level, and so the stage at which a lit-entry event arrives. A tester under the real Attention could see different gating with the same actions.
findings.fix: Add 'with Attention and Horror stubbed to a fixed phase script, or with the level and stage forced equal' to the GIVEN. Add 'counters are never read from restore_epoch'.

findings.finding: R12 says a pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling on RM-DESKTOP (16.6 ms) and RM-DECK (33.3 ms). The AC measures median, p99 and maximum but asserts only the median (<= 0.5 ms) and maximum (<= 2 ms) ceilings, with no p99 or frame-headroom assertion. The values stay pending spike measurement, which is intentional.
findings.fix: State that the frame P99 headroom of R12 (>= 1.7 ms desktop, >= 3.3 ms Deck) is checked by the Pipeline/Kernel perf AC and that this AC only gates Sanity's own step share. Alternatively add a Sanity p99 ceiling placeholder.

findings.finding: The 'was:' comment says 'the repaired_recent stamp is still written, re-enable post-MVP'. Next to the live entry_fields tail ('repaired_recent[] reserved, always empty at MVP', L1027) and G2 this reads as a contradiction. It is a history comment and the live value is correct (value 1).
